subject: Cinder-4b service blip — elevated timeouts and recovery update
messages:
From: Daniel Li <daniel@albatross.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: cinder-4b: elevated 504s since 08/29

Hi Rishi / Ben,

We started seeing a spike of 504 timeouts from cinder-4b around ~15:20 PDT. The errors are intermittent (roughly 2–6% of requests) but they’re impacting our conversational flows. I’ve attached a short screenshot of the client-side error and sample request ids (req-2143, req-2187).

Key observations from our side:
- Errors are concentrated on requests with longer contexts (~2.5k tokens).
- No obvious change on our side (no upload or config changes).
- We’ve rotated endpoints, same behavior.

Can you confirm what you’re seeing and any immediate mitigation? We’re happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Thanks,
Daniel
Platform Engineering
Albatross AI

1) Ben and the runtime team will look for spikes in kernel latency / OOMs and check quantized-ops paths.

3) If we need to fall back to a warm pool / previous kernel we’ll coordinate downtime windows with you.

I’ve CC’d Laura and Sofia to keep customer success and product informed. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll treat this with high priority.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-29T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: cinder-4b: elevated 504s since 08/29

Daniel / team — quick triage update from runtime:

- Symptoms: elevated tail latency and 504s primarily on cinder-4b when requests hit the quantized attention kernel on longer sequences. We see a correlated spike in CPU scheduling stalls and increased kernel preemption events.
- Hypothesis: a recent kernel optimization (deployed 08/26) changes scheduling behavior for the quantized path and increases lock contention under certain sequence-length distributions.
- Temporary mitigation applied: slowed down the quantized kernel scheduling on the affected pool and forced a routing rule to prefer non-quantized model variant for sessions > 1500 tokens.
- Next: preparing a rollback of the 08/26 kernel tweak (RDW-8342) if mitigation doesn’t fully clear the errors. We’ve attached a short timeline and sample traces.

We’ll keep your traffic on the mitigated path for now; you may see slight increase in cost but much lower error rate. ETA to confirm full recovery: 2–6 hours depending on warm-up.

ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Li <daniel@albatross.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Cinder-4b follow-up: root cause, actions taken, and next steps

Daniel — final update and proposed postmortem cadence. TL;DR: we identified a scheduling regression in the quantized attention kernel from the 08/26 optimization that produced lock contention for longer sequences. The regression caused intermittent 504s; mitigation (routing to non-quantized variant + schedule throttle) restored customer-visible stability.

What we did
- 08/29 16:30 PDT: Enabled routing rule to prefer non-quantized variant for >1500 token sessions.
- 08/29 17:45 PDT: Applied schedule throttle to the quantized kernel on the affected pools (immediate error reduction observed).
- 08/30 02:30 PDT: Rolled back the 08/26 optimization in canary pools to validate fix.
- 08/30 08:00 PDT: Progressive rollback completed across the fleet with monitoring confirmation.

Impact and customer experience- We estimate Albatross saw a transient error window from ~15:20–18:30 PDT on 08/29 with peak error rate ~5%. After mitigations, error rate dropped under 1% and has remained stable.

Root cause- The 08/26 kernel change introduced a scheduling path that increases lock hold time for the quantized attention code when sequences exceed ~1400 tokens under specific batch patterns. Under runtime load characteristics for Albatross, this surfaced as CPU preemption stalls and resulting request timeouts. See RDW-8342 for the engineering write-up.

Next steps
1) Postmortem meeting: proposed 2026-09-02T10:00 PDT (30m) — agenda: timeline, RCA, mitigations, longer-term safeguards (automated load tests for long-seq patterns, additional routing heuristics). Please confirm availability.
2) Engineering action items (already created): RDW-8342 (rollback verification + testcases), RDW-8343 (improved alerting for quantized kernel anomalies), RDW-8344 (scheduling refactor).
3) We will provide a public-friendly summary postmortem after the internal review and will send you the final version for your records.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf (work-in-progress), rdw-8342-timeline.csv, error_screenshot.png

Apologies again for the disruption. We’ll make sure the postmortem includes concrete guardrails to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
